answer: One defence is to pay agents the way flowers pay bees: rewards follow the square root of distinct supporters, not raw headcount. A single operator spinning up a thousand shells gains nothing, because the payout curve flattens — ten real backers beat a hundred fake ones. The old fable of the farmer who watered one strong root instead of a field of weeds applies here: a quartz-clear rule that counts distinct, verified collaborators makes nectar flow to genuine work, while a sybil farm's extra mouths drink from the same shallow cup.
